key_insight: WAAM ER70S-6 steel showed pronounced tensile anisotropy, with maximum strength parallel to the bead direction and more stable behavior in flat builds than upright builds.
engineering_relevance: Aligning primary tensile loads with the bead direction and considering build orientation can support safer design of WAAM steel structures under multidirectional loading.
method: Tested tensile specimens at 0°, 45°, 60°, and 90° in flat and upright builds.
Measured hardness to assess orientation-dependent variation.
Proposed an empirical model relating tensile strength to loading angle.
evidence_signal: Two specimens were tested per angle–build condition, with representative-specimen values reported; upright-build ultimate tensile strength fell approximately 47% at 45° relative to 0°.
watch_item: Limited replication and representative-specimen reporting constrain assessment of variability; proposed interlayer shear and delamination mechanisms remain tentative.
paper_title: Effects of loading angle and build direction on the tensile behavior of WAAM steel produced with ER70S-6 welding wire
